mechanism_narrative: A declining trend in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 3.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that dampens economic growth and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a strong labor market coupled with accommodative monetary policy, which together boost corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS have declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high housing starts and strong consumer credit), rising housing starts (HOUST) and rising consumer credit (RSAFS) signal robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion when both HOUST and RSAFS are rising, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE has risen over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that suppresses consumer demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) falls below 115.0, it signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO < 115.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 2100.0 (thousands of units), it signals strong residential demand that boosts construction and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST > 2100.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
